requirements.title: BACKSPACE positions before the current or preceding record and leaves the initial point unchanged
requirements.definition: Execution of BACKSPACE positions the connected file before the current record if one exists, before the preceding record if no current record exists, and leaves the position unchanged at the initial point.

pending.backspace-before-current-record: Create a named sequential file with records A and B, read part or all of the current record as allowed, BACKSPACE, then read into a nonblank sentinel and expect that current record again.
pending.backspace-before-preceding-record: Read known records A then B so there is no current record and B is preceding; BACKSPACE and read into a sentinel, expecting B.
pending.backspace-at-initial-point-unchanged: Open or REWIND a named file to its initial point, BACKSPACE, and read into a sentinel, expecting the first known record.

requirements.title: BACKSPACE after implicit endfile writing positions before the record preceding the endfile record
requirements.definition: If BACKSPACE causes implicit writing of an endfile record, the file is positioned before the record that precedes the endfile record.

pending.backspace-implicit-endfile-before-preced: Write two distinctive sequential records to a named file, perform the operation that requires an implicit endfile record, then BACKSPACE and read; expect the second data record, not marker bytes.

requirements.title: Backspacing a connected nonexistent file is prohibited
requirements.definition: Backspacing a file that is connected but does not exist is prohibited.

requirements.title: Backspacing over list-directed or namelist records is prohibited
requirements.definition: Backspacing over records written using list-directed or namelist formatting is prohibited.

NOTE explains behavior when the preceding record is an endfile record; not normative.
Unnumbered prohibition on backspacing connected nonexistent files.
Unnumbered prohibition on backspacing over list-directed or namelist records.
NOTE gives a BACKSPACE example; not normative.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.5-12.9: termination of data transfer, WAIT, BACKSPACE, ENDFILE, REWIND and FLUSH (batch164). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds. Round 1 found the portable WAIT no-operation cases missing - WAIT with ID=0 (explicitly permitted by 12.7.2 p3) and with ID= omitted on an asynchronous connection with nothing pending must succeed with IOSTAT zero - and an ENDFILE position plan that used REWIND, destroying the state under test; ENDFILE is now observed by the BACKSPACE that 12.8.3 p2 requires before the next transfer, after which a READ must report IOSTAT_END. Seventeen numbered rules were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
